quotes.text: The elders preached a rule: never send nothing; always leave a small ember to fuel future crossings.
half when partners walked steadily, a touch more for audacity guided by memory, and less when caution hardened into fear.
when a partner faltered, patience kept doors open.
If a partner once gave with hesitation, mercy tempered the response; if a partner burned goodwill, discipline drew a line.
balance is a practice, not a rule.
a map of partners who kept faith

note: Nano's River of Triple Light; balance sermons; later 'never send nothing' and less for fear, line for burned goodwill, doors kept open.

quotes.text: But never give nothing—for only through continued offering can anyone find their way back to the sacred proportion.
Not the three vessels I give to the proven fair, nor the nothing I might give to the unrepentant.
Broken patterns receive two, extending hope for redemption.
She filled her vessel halfway and poured.
Those still learning receive measured hope—two or two-and-a-half vessels. But I never send nothing, never betray the cycle.
Thus the keeper's reputation grew
Your constellation spells not one number, but one law: reciprocity matched to what the river brings.
the magic only works when someone dares to give first.
"But doesn't this inconsistency confuse the valleys?" Selene asked.

note: Third Village keeper: three vessels to the fair, two to broken patterns, never nothing; dialogues with the Weaver, Sky, Selene.

quotes.text: We cannot build relationship through escalation or punishment—only through steady proof of who we are.
Send three, even three and a quarter.
send three gold pieces, always three. Return half of what arrives, always half.
Certain captains appeared in her charts repeatedly showing the same signature
Be consistent despite uncertainty. Respond to reality. Recognize patterns that survive distortion.
For today's partner is new, and deserves your authentic measure, not another's punishment.
"Why send the same amount to strangers? You know not their hearts."
The one who gives first takes a risk; the one who returns builds a future.

note: Lighthouse keeper, navigator, bridge builder: send three, return half, never vengeful; meets the Weaver; slight raises for proven partners.

quotes.text: "Send less—two parts of five," the Spirit counseled. "Protect yourself, but give enough to test if patterns can change.
"What if I meet someone whose pattern shows stinginess or greed?"
If your pattern wavers, I send two—protection, but also invitation to grow.
If your constellation shows steady three-part sending and half-returning, I mirror that trust with three coins.
Each giver and receiver left ripples that other travelers could read, revealing past choices as clearly as tracks in sand.
"Always precisely half. That anchor never moves
she could punish the past betrayal and let the valley die, or she could honor his present trust and restore the cycle.
"I see one whose waters returned nothing," she said. "Should I withhold my gift?"

note: Twin Rivers and Mirror: three to the steady, two to wavering or greedy patterns to test change, always half back.

quotes.text: To Valleys who had kept everything, Sky returned less, protecting itself while leaving room for change.
To a Valley who had kept much, Sky still sent enough to test for change.
To Valleys who had kept everything, Sky returned less
Sky sent four drops instead of three-and-a-half, celebrating their proven trustworthiness.
sending three-and-a-half drops, returning half of what was received.
This consistency became Sky's signature, a pattern others could read like stars.
One day, Sky decided to trust.
one scarred by a previous Sky's greed, who had taken the returned mist and sent nothing back.
"Sky, why do you never change? Some days I fear sending, some days I feel bold."

note: Sky and Valley: steady three-and-a-half send, half return; returns less to valleys that kept everything, still tests them; R10 says it never punishes caution.

quotes.text: their neighbors—remembering the broken trust—also kept their water. Soon both banks withered.
their neighbors—remembering the broken trust—also kept their water.
your sending can evolve from three to three-and-a-half, even to four or more, as you meet souls worthy of that trust.
unchanging generosity outward, unchanging fairness inward.
My pattern becomes my reputation, carried by the current to future shores.
she returned half, honoring the pattern regardless of whether her previous partner had honored her.
Perhaps they sent less because noise made them uncertain. Perhaps they're testing. Perhaps they're wounded. It doesn't matter.
"Why maintain this rhythm when partners change like seasons? Why not adapt to each new soul?"

note: Aethera's River of Plenty then Selene's Dual Song; R1 retaliation withers both banks; half returned regardless of past partners.

quotes.text: They do not punish West Village's past selfishness by withholding now.
For new partners or uncertain ones, I send sixty or sixty-five. For those whose marks show proven reliability
"Always half, regardless. That constancy is my foundation.
some partners appeared in market tales showing the same faithful pattern
So they sent back sixty-six sacks. The First Village now held one hundred eleven sacks
I do not punish strangers for others' greed.
"Shouldn't you punish the greedy and reward the generous?"

note: The Weaver's sixty-to-seventy range and fixed half return; repeatedly refuses to punish the greedy; meets River Keeper, Measure and Mirror.

quotes.text: Don't punish today's traveler for yesterday's betrayal.
four-point-eight instead of four-point-five.
"Return the sacred half," she taught, "this is the foundation that cannot bend.
This consistency becomes my reputation, woven into the valley's memory.
Don't punish today's traveler for yesterday's betrayal.
"Why follow these proportions?" asked a young traveler watching.

note: Keeper of Patterns: steady three-to-three-and-a-half send, sacred half return; reads static; slight bonus for proven pattern-walkers.

phrase: the sacred half / sacred proportion: send about three of five, always return half
note: Shared cast: the Weaver's 'sixty to seventy parts' (A7 R4, A3, A2, A4), Measure and Mirror (A4 R8, A7), Selene's Dual Song (A6, A2, A8).
